chapter: Midwest bands: Hardy Brothers, Helvey and Buffalo
title: Joe Thomas and John L. Henderson join the enlarged Vendome band
summary: Joe Thomas, a former waiter picked up by Horace Henderson in Columbus and stranded in Buffalo, became a tenor man in the six-piece Vendome band that swung well.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: You blew it shooting pool. They had a poolroom that stayed open all night. We were playing nine ball for $10.00 a game. And then finally we enlarged the band. We brought in this guy I was telling you about, John L. Henderson, on alto sax, and Joe Thomas, that used to play sax with Jimmy Lunceford.
Because he was in that band too, of Horace Henderson's. So he got stranded there in Buffalo, too.
Yeah. That's why he was around there. See, Joe was a waiter.
Does Joe come from Louisville? He lives in Louisville now, doesn't he?
No, he's out in Kansas City now.
But he was from around Ohio somewhere, around Cleveland, because I saw him, oh, about three or four

months ago in Cleveland. He come in town to see his family. And Horace was looking for a saxophone player, alto sax man, and somebody told him about this guy that played a little sax in Columbus, Ohio. Well, we were in Cleveland, but he told him about this guy in Columbus, said he's a waiter there, at some hotel, but he said he plays pretty good alto, you know. So on our way to West Virginia, Huntington, West Virginia, we stopped and picked up Joe, you know. And Horace could talk you into anything, you know. He was talking about giving up his job and come with the band. So he come. He had a car and everything. We'd shoot firecrackers in the car and we tore it up something awful, you know. Kids, you know.
Finally, when he got stranded he stayed in Buffalo, and then later on this guy started playing tenor, and he turned out to be a great tenor man, you know.

So then we had that band of six pieces, and we had a good band there, with Joe and John and myself, and had a good drummer and everything. We swung very good, and that's all you could think about in those days, was swing, make it move, you know.
And I made that, and I said, well, I'm going to stay right here. So I stayed there, I guess, about two years, and then till things --
